question: Should OpenClaw fail closed before `sessions_send` delivery when propagated inter-agent provenance shows the target agent already participated in the current route?
rationale: The implementation is bounded, but it intentionally changes existing cyclic or revisiting multi-agent routes from delivered runs into returned errors, which is a product and compatibility policy choice.

options.title: Accept fail-closed cycle blocking
options.body: After real runtime proof, rebase, and cleanup, land the provenance-chain guard so A -> B -> C -> A routes stop before the repeated agent run.

options.title: Preserve cyclic revisits
options.body: Reject or rework this direction if legitimate workflows must revisit an agent in the same route without a tool error.

options.title: Require explicit route policy
options.body: Ask for an opt-in, threshold, or documented route policy if maintainers want protection without changing revisit behavior by default.

recommendation.title: Accept fail-closed cycle blocking
recommendation.body: After real runtime proof, rebase, and cleanup, land the provenance-chain guard so A -> B -> C -> A routes stop before the repeated agent run.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete has the strongest observed history across inter-session provenance, A2A policy, and session-tool delivery boundaries.
